question: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 37(1)/(2) minutes and 45 minutes, respectively. Both pipes are open. The cistern will be filled in just half an hour, if the B is turned off after:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total capacity be **LCM(75/2, 45) = 225 units**.

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 225 ÷ (75/2) = **6 units/min**.

Pipe A works for the full **30 minutes** → Work done = 30 × 6 = **180 units**.

Remaining work (to be done by B) = 225 − 180 = **45 units**.

Time for which **Pipe B** was open = 45 ÷ 5 = **9 minutes**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time for **Pipe A** = 75/2 min, Time for **Pipe B** = 45 min. Total time taken = **30 min**.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 Pipe A 75/2 min 225 units 6 
 Pipe B 45 min 5 

⇒ Total capacity of cistern = **225 units**.

⇒ Since **Pipe B** is closed after some time, **Pipe A** remains open for the entire **30 minutes**.

⇒ Water filled by Pipe A in 30 min = 30 × 6 = **180 units**.

⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled by Pipe B = 225 − 180 = **45 units**.

⇒ Time for which Pipe B was open = 45 ÷ 5 = **9 minutes**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to fill the tank. Total Work = Time × Efficiency.

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (+), while outlet/leakage pipes have negative efficiency (−).

Fractional Work Method

If Pipe A fills in x min and Pipe B fills in y min, and B is closed after t min: (30/x) + (t/y) = 1.</p
